recommend.description: proceed: nothing derivable blocks it. amend: a derivable defect in the record. recut: the decomposition does not hold. resurvey: the premise is wrong, not the commitment. ask: stop for a person — the repair is a decision the record may not make for itself (scope, what the intent means, worth at this cost), and an amender would settle it by guessing.

checks.description: Every check defined above, each with what you found. Never empty.

status.description: underivable means you could NOT derive this check — a missing yardstick, not a failed one. Never use broken for something you could not check.

findings.description: Empty when recommending proceed; may be empty when recommending ask. Every entry must cite what it falsifies. On an ask, every finding is still listed — the ones the question covers marked for_person, the derivable ones not.

claim-id.description: The id of the design claim this finding is about — the slug shown in brackets, WITHOUT the brackets. Empty string when the finding is about no single claim, or the design lists invariants with no ids.

check.description: The derived check this finding shows broken. Empty string when it bears on none of them.

for_person.description: true when the only repair for this finding is outside the record — answering the question in asks, deciding scope, filing or naming a follow-up ref, or editing the intent — so an amender handed it would settle it by guessing. false for a derivable defect the record can repair without anyone deciding anything new, which is repaired before the person is asked; a design contradicting a decision the record states is one. Always false unless recommending ask.

confirmed.description: Every claim you were asked to check that you went and checked and found to hold, each with where you read it and whether the code you read already makes it true. By id, not by sentence. Empty when the design lists invariants with no ids.

id.description: The bracketed slug, without the brackets.

evidence.description: The file:line references you read that show it holds. Never empty: a confirmation citing nothing is not counted.

at_this_tree.description: holds: the code you read already makes the claim true. owed: the claim is a sound commitment, and the code you read does not meet it yet — the build has to make it true.

unchecked.description: Each subject you were asked to check and COULD NOT check here, with why — its evidence is not in the code (production data, a deploy history, a service you cannot reach). A subject listed here is ruled on, visibly unconfirmed. Not for a subject you simply did not get to: that one you go and check.

id.description: The bracketed slug, without the brackets.

cause.description: out-of-code: the evidence is not in the code, so no reading of the code can have it. tool-failure: a call you made to a tool you needed was denied or errored here — only one you made and saw fail, never one you expect to be refused; try it first. Your transcript is checked, and a tool-failure it does not show is read as plain unchecked.

relation_rulings.description: One ruling per baseline id listed under relation-honest — every one of them, and nothing else. Empty only when the prompt lists none.

id.description: The baseline id as listed, without the brackets.

cause.description: Empty unless the prompt shows a previous ruling on this id and this ruling differs from it. Then: what moved since that ruling and makes it wrong — in the record, in the code, or in an objection shown to you. A reversal with no cause, on an id whose record did not move, is not taken.

ruling.description: breaks: this design stops the id being true of the area, so it belongs under :breaks. stands: it is still true once this design is built.

reason.description: Why — for stands, what keeps it true; for breaks, what in the design moves it.

asks.description: The question the human still has to answer, with everything derived taken off the table. Required on ask; on any other recommendation empty when nothing is left for a person to decide. Never answer it yourself.

asks_about.description: The id of every design claim whose ruling the person's answer to asks decides — the slug shown in brackets, WITHOUT the brackets. Never shown to the person. Empty when asks decides no claim.

questions.description: Each separate question or alternative asks poses, one entry each, in the order asks poses them. Empty when asks is empty.

id.description: The id of the STILL OPEN question this entry keeps, as shown, when it asks that question again — in its words or new ones. Empty string for a question nothing open asked.

text.description: The question or alternative, as the person reads it.

settled_questions.description: Each STILL OPEN question you do not keep in questions, with the record change that settled it. Empty when nothing is shown still open.

id.description: The id of the STILL OPEN question, as shown.

by.description: The change to the record since it was asked that settles it: the claim or clause, and what it now says.

clause_rulings.description: One ruling per clause listed under THE CLAUSES, by its key — every one of them. A subject confirmed or found against while one of its listed clauses has no ruling here is an incomplete judgment, and is not counted. Empty only when the prompt lists no clauses.

clause.description: The clause's key as listed, `<id>#<n>`, without brackets.

ruling.description: held: the clause is true of the code — for a `refuted by` clause, the counterexample it names exists nowhere. false: it is not, and a finding against the subject names it.

evidence.description: The file:line references you read to rule it: where it holds, or the counterexample's site. A held clause citing nothing is not counted.

search.description: On a held clause marked (search owed): the search over the WHOLE tree, tests included, that found nothing to deny it — the pattern and the root it ran from. A held clause marked (search owed) with this empty is not counted. Empty on any other clause.

step_back.description: Each area you step back on this round, one entry each: an area the prompt shows as hot, whose repeated findings say its approach is off. Empty when you step back on none.

area.description: The hot area's id, as shown, WITHOUT the brackets.

step.description: restate: the amender restates the area's approach; recut / resurvey: the step your recommend takes; ask: your asks puts the area-level question to the person.

classes.description: The classes of finding that kept landing in the area, each a short phrase.
